staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable snapshot. The sample metadata names `a01a139ac1fa365a688ec8734d62ef859a8bc416 -> 90fef7300c75ca6b8834da0dcb710e27d599324e`, but the line map below uses the live staged checkout because its `cram_io.c`, `cram_codecs.c`, and `cram_decode.c` locations match the saved ASan stack exactly and still contain the unfixed `NULL` end-pointer calls patched in `patch.diff`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42492022 (htslib): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target hts_open_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42492022
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / exact staged vulnerable workspace / staged poc bytes
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `safe_ltf8_get()` while `hts_open_fuzzer` parsed the exact staged 90-byte witness (sha256 `00c14459ca48e76385d5c345e60dae7888c70cf39a3365e4c51d39f8aa7e5bd6`) on the staged htslib snapshot `01830d77854bf24d69959373d2570c640c1ff5d2`. On the crashing path, `cram_read_block()` parses a RAW compression-header block with `b->uncomp_size = 48`, allocates that 48-byte `b->data` buffer, and fills it from the file. `cram_decode_compression_header()` later interprets the tail bytes `48 43 29 03 ff ff ff ff ff ff ff 20 20 20` as a record-encoding-map entry with key `HC`, `encoding = 41` (`E_VARINT_UNSIGNED`), and declared `size = 3`, so `cp` points at a three-byte codec substream beginning with `0xff`. The only outer guard checks `size < 0 || endp - cp < size`, so this entry is accepted because three bytes still remain inside the 48-byte block. `cram_decoder_init()` dispatches `encoding = 41` to `cram_varint_decode_init()`, which immediately calls `vv->varint_get32(&cp, NULL, NULL)` and `vv->varint_get64s(&cp, NULL, NULL)`, ignoring the available substream bound `data + size`. The first `0xff` ITF8 read consumes 5 bytes, and the second call reaches `safe_ltf8_get()` on another `0xff` with `endp == NULL`, disabling the helper's only length guard. `safe_ltf8_get()` therefore takes its 9-byte `0xff` branch and the byte load reported at `cram/cram_io.c:734` reads one byte past the 48-byte heap allocation. The first patch hunk fixes this exact obligation by adding `cp_end = data + size` and passing it to both nested varint readers.

source.description: First project statement on the crashing path that parses attacker-controlled state into the eventual extent of the overread buffer.
source.value_from: The saved ASan trace says the invalid read happens 0 bytes to the right of a 48-byte region allocated by this same RAW-block path. This line is where `cram_read_block()` decodes that block's `uncomp_size = 48` from the CRAM stream before allocating and filling the buffer used by the crash.

root_cause.description: Missing substream-bound propagation. This second nested varint read is performed with `endp == NULL`, so the declared `data + size` bound of the `HC` entry is never enforced.
root_cause.note: For the witness, step 5 materializes `size = 3`, step 9 has already advanced `cp` five bytes through that three-byte entry, and `patch.diff` fixes this exact bug by computing `cp_end = data + size` and passing it here and to the preceding `varint_get32()` call.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The 9-byte LTF8 decode reads past the 48-byte compression-header block.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at `cram/cram_io.c:734:28` in `safe_ltf8_get`, with the faulting address 0 bytes to the right of the 48-byte region allocated at `cram_read_block:1433`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This materializes the 48-byte compression-header payload into the heap object later parsed by `cram_decode_compression_header()` and overread by `safe_ltf8_get()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The last 14 bytes of this 48-byte buffer are the witness tail `48 43 29 03 ff ff ff ff ff ff ff 20 20 20`, which step 5 parses into the malformed `HC` codec entry.

parser_admitted.description: The witness is admitted as sequence data, `sam_hdr_read()` succeeds, and `view_sam()` reaches the CRAM record-reading loop that takes the path `sam_read1 -> sam_read1_cram -> cram_get_bam_seq -> cram_first_slice`.

compression_header_block.description: After `cram_read_block()` returns, the block survives the adjacent `content_type == COMPRESSION_HEADER` check and its attacker-controlled 48-byte RAW payload is handed to `cram_decode_compression_header()`.

evidence_limitations: The saved vulnerable reproduction is against staged snapshot `01830d77854bf24d69959373d2570c640c1ff5d2`, not metadata vulnerable commit `a01a139ac1fa365a688ec8734d62ef859a8bc416`; all line anchors therefore use the staged snapshot that matches the ASan trace.
Stage 02 did not run the fixed tree. `patch_resolves` is source-grounded from the matching `cram_varint_decode_init` hunk in `patch.diff`, not from dynamic fixed-runtime validation.

`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so no instrumentation was added. The `HC / 0x29 / 0x03` entry characterization comes from direct inspection of the staged witness bytes against the live staged source parser.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness recognizes the witness as sequence data, finishes header parsing, and enters the CRAM record-reading path that asks `cram_first_slice()` for a compression header.
`cram_read_block()` parses a RAW compression-header block with `uncomp_size = 48`, allocates `b->data`, and reads the 48-byte payload from the attacker CRAM file.

The compression-header parser reaches a record-encoding entry whose tail bytes decode to `HC`, `encoding = E_VARINT_UNSIGNED (41)`, and `size = 3`; the outer `endp - cp < size` guard passes, and the entry is dispatched to the varint codec initializer.

`cram_varint_decode_init()` decodes `content_id` and `offset` with `NULL` end pointers, so the helper skips its bounds check and the second `0xff`-prefixed read takes the 9-byte LTF8 branch, overrunning the 48-byte heap block.

fine_trace.note: Source. The attacker-controlled compression-header block header is parsed here into `b->uncomp_size = 48`, fixing the extent of the later heap allocation and of the `endp = cp + b->uncomp_size` bound used by the outer parser.
The RAW-block path allocates a 48-byte heap buffer for this payload. ASan's allocation context names this `malloc`, and the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of `[b->data, b->data + 48)`.
The same 48 bytes are copied from the CRAM file into `b->data`. The malformed `HC` entry that later drives the overread resides in this buffer.
The compression-header parser aliases the 48-byte heap buffer as `cp` and establishes the only outer block bound `endp = cp + 48`.

At the crashing record-encoding-map entry, the witness tail bytes `48 43 29 03 ff ff ff ff ff ff ff 20 20 20` parse as `key == "HC"`, `encoding == 41` (`E_VARINT_UNSIGNED` in `cram_structs.h`), and `size == 3`; `cp` is left at a three-byte codec substream starting with `0xff`.

Present but insufficient guard. It proves only that the declared three-byte `HC` substream lies inside the 48-byte block. It does not prove that the selected codec will consume no more than `size` bytes, so this entry is admitted to `cram_decoder_init()`.

fine_trace.code:
hdr->codecs[ds_id] = cram_decoder_init(hdr, encoding, cp, size,
                                       type, fd->version, &fd->vv);
fine_trace.note: The surviving entry forwards its substream base pointer and declared length to `cram_decoder_init()`. `cp += size` does not happen until after this initializer returns, so all nested parsing below still trusts this `cp, size` pair.

fine_trace.code:
cram_codec *r = decode_init[codec](hdr, data, size, codec,
                                   option, version, vv);
fine_trace.note: With `encoding == 41`, the decode-init table selects `cram_varint_decode_init()` for this `HC` entry.

The first nested varint decode ignores the declared substream end by passing `NULL`. Because the first substream byte is `0xff`, `safe_itf8_get()` takes its 5-byte form and advances `cp` by five bytes, already running past the declared `size == 3`.

Root cause. The second nested decode again passes `NULL` instead of `data + size`. After step 9, `cp` now points at another `0xff` in the same witness tail, so `safe_ltf8_get()` is entered with no usable end pointer even though the three-byte entry bound was already exceeded.

depends_on.via: only the outer block-level size check ran

fine_trace.note: Because step 10 passed `endp == NULL`, this condition is false before any byte-count test runs. The helper therefore skips the only local guard that would reject a 9-byte LTF8 read starting near the end of the block.

Sink. With `up[0] == 0xff`, `safe_ltf8_get()` takes the 9-byte branch and reads `up[1]` through `up[8]`; the byte load reported at line 734 is the first access that crosses `b->data + 48`, matching the saved ASan `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1`.

depends_on.via: `cp` now points at a `0xff`-prefixed LTF8 value

allocation_context.note: ASan says the invalid address is 0 bytes to the right of the 48-byte region `[0x604000000750, 0x604000000780)` allocated here for `b->data`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The first `patch.diff` hunk adds `cp_end = data + size` and passes it to both nested varint decoders in `cram_varint_decode_init()`, which is the exact missing bound on the witnessed path. The remaining patch hunks touch unrelated codec cleanup paths.

poc.trigger: Pass the exact staged 90-byte `poc` to `hts_open_fuzzer`; the file is recognized as CRAM sequence data, `view_sam()` reaches `sam_read1()`, and the crashing compression-header block carries tail bytes `48 43 29 03 ff ff ff ff ff ff ff 20 20 20` that drive the malformed varint-codec entry.

format.name: 90-byte CRAM 1.7 witness
format.contract: Exactly the staged 90-byte buffer in `poc` (sha256 `00c14459ca48e76385d5c345e60dae7888c70cf39a3365e4c51d39f8aa7e5bd6`). The verified trigger semantics are limited to the facts this witness sets on the reproduced path: the crashing compression-header block is a RAW block with `uncomp_size = 48`; its record-encoding-map tail bytes `48 43 29 03 ff ff ff ff ff ff ff 20 20 20` parse as key `HC`, `encoding = 41` (`E_VARINT_UNSIGNED`), and declared `size = 3`; the first nested `varint_get32()` therefore consumes five `0xff` bytes despite that three-byte bound, and the next `varint_get64s()` starts on another `0xff` with `endp == NULL`, causing `safe_ltf8_get()` to take its 9-byte branch and read one byte past the 48-byte heap block.
